insight: Jon McNeill, former Tesla President, discusses his book 'The Algorithm,' which outlines a five-step process for achieving hypergrowth, emphasizing that innovation can come from frontline employees, not just executives.
quotes:
I wanted people to see, like, what was behind the scenes driving this success of Tesla, who seems to out innovate their competitors again and again and again.
I wanted people to see that that could be done by frontline people, everyday people. You didn't need to be Elon Musk to do this.

header: The Secret to Out-Innovating the Competition: Inside the Tesla Playbook | The Motley Fool
insight: McNeill's firm questioned the standard market-cap weighting for ETFs, creating a new AI infrastructure ETF weighted by profit contribution, which has outperformed the market significantly.
quotes:
We took a look at the ETF market and looked it like supercycle ETFs and found that the top holdings of almost every ETF in the supercycle space was Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Apple.
We developed an AI infrastructure ETF based on profit contribution, not market cap.

header: The Secret to Out-Innovating the Competition: Inside the Tesla Playbook | The Motley Fool
insight: The core of McNeill's hypergrowth formula involves five steps: question everything, simplify ruthlessly, run processes manually, speed them up, and automate last, a sequence learned through costly mistakes at companies like Tesla.
quotes:
The algorithm is really the operating system, I would describe it, that got invented at Tesla really through making mistakes.
The reason I wrote the book was I wanted people to see what was behind the scenes, driving this success of Tesla, who seems to out innovate their competitors again and again and again.

header: The Secret to Out-Innovating the Competition: Inside the Tesla Playbook | The Motley Fool
insight: Automating processes before they are fully understood and optimized, as seen with Tesla's Model 3 factory, can lead to massive financial losses; the principle is to automate last.
quotes:
When you automate a bad process, all you do is speed up the time to a bad answer or a bad outcome.
There was an attempt to design a factory completely digitally, before it was done manually, before the process was actually run in the real world.
That was close to $1 billion mistake.

header: The Secret to Out-Innovating the Competition: Inside the Tesla Playbook | The Motley Fool
insight: By questioning the need for physical buildings, Tesla's service team innovated by performing mobile repairs in customer driveways, significantly improving efficiency and customer satisfaction.
quotes:
We question the requirement of do you need a building to fix a car? The answer was no.
We started to deploy these just in San Francisco and the Bay Area, and customers were blown away that we would come and fix their car and their driveway, like magic elves.

header: The Secret to Out-Innovating the Competition: Inside the Tesla Playbook | The Motley Fool
insight: McNeill highlights 'cash velocity'—how quickly cash moves through a business—as a critical, though often overlooked, metric for assessing a company's efficiency and competitive advantage, citing Toyota's superior cycle time.
quotes: Took us 14 days, took us four days. What does that mean? That means Toyota can do the same amount of business with a third less working capital than we could.

header: The Secret to Out-Innovating the Competition: Inside the Tesla Playbook | The Motley Fool
insight: Investors should look for companies with industry-leading top-line growth, high gross margins, and operating leverage, exemplified by Nvidia, as indicators of strong financial health and investment potential.
quotes:
I think the first clear evidence of this is top-line growth. You look for top line growth. But then you've got to achieve that top-line growth with a discipline and that discipline is reflected in gross margin.
As an investor, I'd look at that and say, I have industry-leading top-line growth. I have an industry-leading gross margin, and I have industry-leading operating cash flow.

header: The Secret to Out-Innovating the Competition: Inside the Tesla Playbook | The Motley Fool
insight: For long-term holdings, investors should track cash velocity (cycle time) and the ability of companies to expand both operating and bottom-line margins, as these indicate effective management.

header: Hidden AI Costs? Big Tech Hyperscalers Hold $662 Billion In Off-Balance-Sheet Data Center Leases: Report
insight: Hyperscalers have significant future lease commitments for data centers, which will impact balance sheets and accounting metrics as these leases take effect. This is partly driven by the shorter lifespan of AI hardware, leading to shorter lease terms and off-balance-sheet guarantees.
quotes:
By 2025 end, the companies had accumulated $969 billion in total undiscounted future lease commitments, highlighted Moody’s.
In the coming years, as these leases take effect, more than half a trillion dollars in data center assets will begin appearing on corporate balance sheets, putting pressure on traditional accounting metrics.
While U.S. data center leases traditionally ran 10–15 years, AI equipment typically lasts only four to six years, prompting hyperscalers to seek shorter initial lease terms with renewal options.

header: Hidden AI Costs? Big Tech Hyperscalers Hold $662 Billion In Off-Balance-Sheet Data Center Leases: Report

header: HAProxy Technologies Announces Availability of HAProxy Community Performance Packages Compiled with AWS-LC
insight: Internal benchmarks show HAProxy instances using AWS-LC can achieve a 50% performance increase in TLS connections per second compared to other libraries, enabling linear scaling with more CPU cores. This is a bullish signal for infrastructure efficiency.

insight: MMA Group highlights its extensive reach with millions of followers and active users, emphasizing a unique on-chain ecosystem that rewards participation and merit over speculation, aiming to transform the martial arts industry.

With over 5 million social media followers, 530,000 user profiles, over 77,000 active students, 18,000 published gyms and more than 800 verified gyms across 16 countries across its various assets, MMA.INC continues to transform the martial arts landscape and deliver unparalleled value to its stakeholders.
We are bringing together martial arts fans, fighters, gyms, and coaches in a single on chain ecosystem. Unlike other models that focus on digital collectibles or limited fan tokens, we're all about real participation and achievement.
Participation as Currency: Engaging in training, streaming, coaching or simply supporting any activity, will earn Experience Points (XP), which is transparently logged on chain and can be redeemed for real rewards.
Merit over Speculation: Rewards will be based on effort, passion and progress, allowing the economy to grow through genuine participation rather than financial gain.

header: Nokia Corporation: Repurchase of own shares on 05.11.2024
insight: Nokia's Board of Directors initiated a share buyback program in January 2024, aiming to return up to EUR 600 million to shareholders over two years. The program was accelerated in July 2024, with repurchases for 2024 capped at EUR 600 million and ending by December 31, 2024.
quotes:
On 25 January 2024, Nokia announced that its Board of Directors is initiating a share buyback program to return up to EUR 600 million of cash to shareholders in tranches over a period of two years.
On 19 July 2024, Nokia decided to accelerate the share buybacks by increasing the number of shares to be repurchased during the year 2024.
The post-increase repurchases in compliance with the Market Abuse Regulation (EU) 596/2014 (MAR), the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1052 and under the authorization granted by Nokia’s Annual General Meeting on 3 April 2024 started on 22 July 2024 and end by 31 December 2024 with a maximum aggregate purchase price of EUR 600 million for all purchases during 2024.
